label: Lakehouse (Iceberg, Unity Catalog)

scripts.name: LAKEHOUSE_SCAN
scripts.sql:
CREATE OR REPLACE RUST SCALAR SCRIPT {schema}.LAKEHOUSE_SCAN(common VARCHAR(2000000), files VARCHAR(2000000))
EMITS (...) AS
%udf_object {udf_object}
/

scripts.name: LAKEHOUSE_VERSION
scripts.sql:
CREATE OR REPLACE RUST SCALAR SCRIPT {schema}.LAKEHOUSE_VERSION()
RETURNS VARCHAR(100) AS
%udf_object {udf_object}
/

scripts.name: LAKEHOUSE_DISTRIBUTE_FILES
scripts.sql:
CREATE OR REPLACE LUA SET SCRIPT {schema}.LAKEHOUSE_DISTRIBUTE_FILES(files VARCHAR(2000000))
EMITS (files VARCHAR(2000000)) AS
function run(ctx)
    repeat
        ctx.emit(ctx.files)
    until not ctx.next()
end
/

secret_label: S3 secret key, or catalog token

inputs.label: Storage region (the bucket's AWS region, e.g. us-east-2; Unity Catalog needs it)
S3 access key ID (empty: a catalog token with vended credentials)
S3 secret key, or catalog token

failures.pattern: EXTERNAL[ _]USE[ _]SCHEMA|External Data Access from non Databricks Compute|SCHEMA_DB_STORAGE
Max catalog version is required|catalog-managed table

catalog_managed.message: A table in {namespace} is catalog-managed: Databricks keeps its newest commits in Unity Catalog, and this adapter version cannot read such a table yet.
catalog_managed.hint: An Iceberg table (or a Delta table with Iceberg reads on) reads fine through Databricks' Iceberg REST endpoint, which follows the Iceberg metadata instead: exakit connect lakehouse --url https://{host}/api/2.1/unity-catalog/iceberg-rest with EXAKIT_VS_WAREHOUSE=<catalog> and EXAKIT_VS_NAMESPACE=<schema>. Any table reads through the SQL warehouse: exakit connect databricks.

region.message: The storage answered from another AWS region than {region}.
region.hint: Give the bucket's own region (S3 console, bucket properties): set EXAKIT_VS_REGION and run exakit connect lakehouse --name {name|lower} again.

external_access.message: Unity Catalog does not let engines outside Databricks read the files of {namespace}.
external_access.hint: The metastore needs External data access switched on, and the token's user needs EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA on the schema. A schema on Databricks Default Storage (Free Edition, serverless-only workspaces) can never be read from outside: give it a managed location on your own storage, or read it through the SQL warehouse instead: exakit connect databricks

auth.message: The catalog or the storage refused the credentials.
auth.hint: Check the S3 access key ({user}) and its secret key, or the catalog token. A 403 from storage can also be a bucket policy that does not let this key read the table's files.

network.message: The database cannot reach the catalog at {host}:{port} or the storage that holds the table's files ({endpoint}).
network.hint: Both are reached from INSIDE the database container, not from this PC. Something on this computer is reached as localhost (the kit uses the container's host alias); check that the catalog and the storage answer on the ports given.

schema_missing.message: The catalog has no namespace named {namespace}.
schema_missing.hint: Check the namespace (Unity Catalog: catalog.schema); re-run connect with EXAKIT_VS_NAMESPACE.

permission.message: The storage refused to let the key read the table's files.
permission.hint: Grant the access key read access to the bucket, then: exakit source check {name|lower}

notes: Table and column names arrive upper-cased (ORDERS, ORDER_ID): query them without quotes.
Iceberg tables with equality deletes, or ORC or Avro data files, are not read; positional deletes and deletion vectors are.
Filters, projections, LIMIT and aggregates run inside the Rust scan; nothing is copied into Exasol.

Databricks tables are reachable here too, without a SQL warehouse. Iceberg tables (or Delta tables with Iceberg reads on) through Databricks' Iceberg REST endpoint: --url https://<workspace-host>/api/2.1/unity-catalog/iceberg-rest, EXAKIT_VS_WAREHOUSE=<catalog>, EXAKIT_VS_NAMESPACE=<schema>, a personal access token (no --user) and EXAKIT_VS_REGION; Delta tables through exakit connect unity --url https://<workspace-host> with a personal access token (no --user), EXAKIT_VS_NAMESPACE=<catalog>.<schema> and EXAKIT_VS_REGION=<the bucket's AWS region>. The schema must live on your own storage with external data access allowed; otherwise use exakit connect databricks.
